chunks: A believer from the House of Pharaoh who had kept his faith to himself, said: 'Will you kill a man because he says: My Lord is God, when he has brought clear signs from his Lord to you? If he is a liar his lie will recoil back on him; but in case he speaks the truth, what he predicts will befall you. Surely God does not show the way to the shameful liar.'
ai.seo_question: Who was the believer from the House of Pharaoh and what did he say about killing Moses?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this figure is often identified as 'Al-Haqq' (The Truth) or a prominent member of the Banu Israel who concealed his faith (Taqiyyah) to protect the Prophet. His argument establishes the principle of validating prophethood through clear signs (Bayyinat) while assigning the burden of proof to the claimant, a concept central to Shia theological debates on Imamate. The verse highlights the courage of the 'secret believer' who stood against the tyranny of Pharaoh, serving as a model for early Shia communities under Umayyad and Abbasid rule.
